s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye following a traumatic incident to the head
salient_findings: Decreased vision in one eye after being struck by lightning
Central macular thickening on fundus examination at 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in the affected eye at 7 weeks
key_facts: Patient is a white woman in her 20s
Unremarkable medical and ocular history
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
Struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
Central macular thickening was observed at 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract was visible at 7 weeks
Spectral-domain OCT showed subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers at initial examination
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption were observed at 2 weeks
Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities was observed at 7 weeks

differentials: Commotio retinae with retinal pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Commotio retinae with retinal pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Commotio retinae
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced traumatic incident to the head and presented with decreased vision, consistent with commotio retinae

shortlist.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of direct lightning strike to the forehead and subsequent vision loss suggests traumatic optic neuropathy

shortlist.label: Lightning-induced maculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and OCT findings, including cystoid macular edema and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption, are consistent with lightning-induced maculopathy

shortlist.label: Traumatic cataract
shortlist.why_kept: Development of mild posterior subcapsular cataract at 7 weeks post-injury is consistent with traumatic cataract

shortlist.label: Cystoid macular edema
shortlist.why_kept: OCT findings of intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption support the diagnosis of cystoid macular edema

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms began after being struck by lightning, and the progression of macular changes, including central macular thickening and intraretinal cystoid changes, are consistent with lightning-induced maculopathy.

rejected.label: Commotio retinae
rejected.why: Commotio retinae typically presents with immediate vision loss and retinal edema, which is not consistent with the patient's initial normal fundus examination.

rejected.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: Traumatic optic neuropathy would likely present with a relative afferent pupillary defect, which is not present in this patient.

rejected.label: Traumatic cataract
rejected.why: While the patient did develop a cataract, it was not the primary presenting symptom, and the macular changes are more consistent with lightning-induced maculopathy.

rejected.label: Cystoid macular edema
rejected.why: Cystoid macular edema is a possible complication of lightning-induced maculopathy, but it does not fully explain the patient's symptoms and the progression of macular changes.
